claims.statement: Ashoka was the third Mauryan emperor. He supported Buddhism and had inscriptions placed across his empire. These surviving texts make his rule unusually visible. They let us compare what a king said about government and conduct with the monuments and places connected to his reign.
Ashoka’s reign: 273 BCE to 232 BCE. Reign, not lifespan. The Met uses c.273–232 BCE; Livius gives accession in 272. Accession and coronation chronologies differ. No birth date is inferred.
